newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

A conflict between the KAFCO management and the workers-employees union has created a volatile situation in the Karnaphuli Fertiliser Company, officials of the joint-venture enterprise complained to the government.
Some ruling Awami League lawmakers yesterday criticised the government for "dismal" situation in marketing and distribution of fertiliser throughout the country.

A permanent agreement is likely to be reached between the government and the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS) for a lasting peace in the Chittagong Hill Tracts during talks scheduled to be held in Dhaka on Saturday.

Secretary-general of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, yesterday blamed India for pursuing the policy of keeping its dominance in the region through the proposed sub-regional cooperation.
The people across the country experienced worst power failure for the second day on Wednesday due to drastic fall in power generation in different plants of the Power Development Board (PDB).

Chief health officer of Dhaka City Corporation Dr. Mohammad Afsaruddin and six assistant health officers responsible for eradicating mosquitoes were suspended on Wednesday for negligence of duty and misconduct.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange has turned down appeals of six different companies, which recently went public, for listing in the bourse.

Opposition members of parliament yesterday accused the government of damaging the capital market, but Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria claimed the current slide in the market is only a "large correction."
